scope: Read-only official documentation research. No app/account/token/key/installation/Worker creation, external mutation, secret access, tests or frozen-source edits.
recommended_route: Repository-owner private GitHub App + Worker installation-token authentication. End users need no GitHub or provider account; the maintainer needs GitHub and a hosting account.

fine_grained_bot_PAT_result.reason: GitHub documents that fine-grained PATs cannot contribute to public repositories where the token owner is not a member, or to outside/repository-collaborator repositories. A bot account does not own the separate personal account EinarOlafsson/spacr. Adding the bot as collaborator does not repair this limitation.
fine_grained_bot_PAT_result.required_spec_correction: features/new/700_anonymous_error_reports_without_a_github_account.txt lines27–30 currently prescribe that unsupported fine-grained bot token. Replace the design in the normal held N700 integration, not frozen CI source.

step_by_step.action: Sign into the existing EinarOlafsson account, which owns spacr. A separate bot account is unnecessary. Open https://github.com/settings/apps/new.

Choose a globally unique app name such as spacr-first-responder, with homepage https://github.com/EinarOlafsson/spacr. Leave OAuth callback, user authorization during installation and device flow unused. Disable webhook Active for this outbound-only relay.

Under Repository permissions, set Issues to Read & write. Leave Contents, Actions, Administration and all other optional permissions at No access; Metadata read is mandatory/default. Under Where can this GitHub App be installed choose Only on this account, then Create GitHub App.
step_by_step.note: The app lives on EinarOlafsson, not on a separate bot account. An app owned elsewhere would need Any account/public visibility before Einar could install it.

step_by_step.action: In app settings, record its Client ID and App ID (non-secret). Current GitHub docs place key generation under Credentials → Key pairs → New key. Download and retain the PEM privately. Never send it in chat, put it in Git, or distribute it in spaCR.

App settings → Install App → Install beside EinarOlafsson → Only select repositories → spacr → Install. Record the installation ID from the installed app settings URL or let the Worker discover it using the app-authenticated GET /repos/EinarOlafsson/spacr/installation.

Prepare a Cloudflare Worker that supports GitHub App authentication. These proposed variable names must match that implementation: GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY=EinarOlafsson/spacr, and the secret GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY. Existing N700 source is a specification, not a deployed relay; this integration still needs implementation and testing.

Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages → chosen Worker → Settings → Variables and Secrets → Add → type Secret. Add the complete private PEM under GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, then Deploy when the tested Worker is ready. Non-secret IDs can be ordinary variables. Add secrets directly on the platform, not through chat.

If native Web Crypto imports PKCS#8, handle GitHub’s downloaded PKCS#1 PEM correctly. Either use a compatible tested signer or convert locally with openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in app-private-key.pem -out app-private-key.pkcs8.pem, and store the converted key as the Worker secret. The conversion is proposed, not executed.

Inside the Worker, sign an RS256 JWT with iss=Client ID, iat=now−60 seconds and exp no more than 10 minutes ahead. Authenticate GitHub requests using Authorization: Bearer JWT, Accept: application/vnd.github+json, User-Agent and the current documented API-version header (currently 2026-03-10).

POST /app/installations/{installation_id}/access_tokens with {"repositories":["spacr"],"permissions":{"issues":"write"}}. Cache the token server-side until shortly before returned expires_at; installation tokens expire after 1 hour. Never return the token to spaCR.

With that installation token, POST /repos/EinarOlafsson/spacr/issues with validated title/body for a new redacted report; for a known signature, POST /repos/EinarOlafsson/spacr/issues/{number}/comments. Keep owner/repo fixed server-side and validate issue identity. Reports are authored by the app, not impersonated as the anonymous user. Verify label application in acceptance rather than assuming every token can set labels.

Before exposing the endpoint, validate schema and size, redact again, implement bounded rate limits and atomic deduplication, and test one approved synthetic report plus a duplicate. Confirm one issue and one duplicate comment, selected repo only, no secrets in payload/logs/client, opt-out sends nothing, and failure queues bounded reports. Link the HTTPS endpoint from spaCR only after the held integration passes; any real test issue posting requires its own explicit authorization.
step_by_step.note: This is the proposed N700 product acceptance, not a live service or completed test.

alternatives.valid: Can target the owner’s own spacr repo with Issues write and no Contents write; valid because owner is same account.
alternatives.tradeoff: Personal credential tied to maintainer lifecycle; App preferred for a long-lived service. Not the original separate-bot account proposal.

alternatives.route: Dedicated bot account classic PAT with public_repo
alternatives.valid: Classic PAT supports writes to public repositories outside its own account. It can create public issues with the rights of that account.
alternatives.tradeoff: public_repo is not issues-only and cannot be restricted to one repository. It includes broader public code/repository abilities where the bot has access. Full repo scope additionally grants private-repository access and is unnecessary for this public issue relay. Adding collaborator grants broader rights; do not call that safe least privilege.

cloud_AI_boundary: GitHub App authentication supplies issue filing only. Free cloud AI requires a separately configured maintainer-hosted inference service with quotas. It does not give end users a provider subscription, and unlimited free inference must not be promised. Root’s cloud-AI research lane owns the current quota/model recommendation.
user_can_do_now: Create the owner-owned GitHub App with exactly Issues Read & write and selected spacr installation.
Keep the private PEM locally or upload directly to a ready Worker secret; do not share it in chat.
Share only Client ID/App ID/installation ID and desired non-secret Worker URL with the integration lane.
Cloudflare account setup is needed only for the maintainer; end users need no account.
developer_remaining: Implement/test the Worker App JWT token exchange and fixed-repository report route; production code currently does not contain a deployed anonymous relay. No public issue or Worker deployment performed.
